name: useThermometer
summary: Discovery of the non-contact infrared temperature sensor on Google Pixel Pro hardware; temperatures stay null until a verified decoder exists.
plain: Finds out whether this phone lists the far-infrared temperature sensor that Pixel Pro models carry. It does not read a temperature from it yet, so the temperatures are always null and the reason is in error.
description: The native module asks Android SensorManager for a sensor whose type string contains object_temperature or mlx90632, or whose name contains Thermometer or MLX90632, and reports its name in sensorName. PixelKit has no verified decoder for that sensor's samples (unit and channel layout), so surfaceTemperatureC, surfaceTemperatureF and ambientTemperatureC are null and error states which sensor was found and why nothing is read. There is no emissivity or measurement-mode setting: nothing downstream of the sensor would apply it. Nothing is estimated or simulated.

returns.name: isSupported
returns.desc: Whether SensorManager lists a far-infrared temperature sensor on this device.

returns.name: surfaceTemperatureC
returns.desc: Surface temperature in degrees Celsius (°C); null because no decoder exists.

returns.name: surfaceTemperatureF
returns.desc: Surface temperature in degrees Fahrenheit (°F); null because no decoder exists.

returns.name: ambientTemperatureC
returns.desc: Sensor die / ambient temperature in degrees Celsius (°C); null because no decoder exists.

returns.name: sensorName
returns.desc: Name SensorManager gives the sensor, or null when none was found.

returns.name: error
returns.desc: Why temperatures are null: the sensor was found but is not decoded, no sensor is listed, or the probe failed.

returns.name: source
returns.desc: 'hardware' when a temperature was read, otherwise 'unavailable'.

agentNote: Never show a temperature from this hook unless surfaceTemperatureC is a number; today it is null on every device, with the reason in error. Do not offer emissivity or mode controls: the hook has none.
